editorial:
After Ellen Graham dies, her daughter Annie tries to hold her family together while strange things start happening around the house. Toni Collette plays Annie with raw emotion, and the kids, especially Milly Shapiro as Charlie, add a creepy feeling without needing cheap jump scares. The movie moves slowly at first, letting grief and family tension build, then turns into a nightmare that feels personal and hard to shake. You are not just watching monsters; you are watching a family fall apart under secrets they never asked for.

The acting is the big reason to watch, especially Collette, who makes every scene feel real and painful. The camera work and sound design create dread, but some viewers may find the slow pace and heavy sadness too much. If you like horror that gets under your skin instead of just loud shocks, this is for you. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best picture and sound.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Annie is possessed and kills herself by cutting off her own head. Peter runs to the treehouse, where cult members have gathered around Charlie's decapitated body and a crowned figure. They bow to Peter, revealing that Charlie was really the demon Paimon and the family was being used to give him a male host. Peter is crowned as Paimon's new body, and the cult celebrates.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves slow-burn horror and family drama.
